C0.quote: friends choosing a restaurant may utilize a voting procedure
C0.note: Public decision-making / perpetual voting: mechanisms aggregate agents' valuations into a sequence of collective decisions.

C1.quote: we analyze the fairness of three known mechanisms
C1.note: Results concern which mechanisms satisfy which fairness or efficiency properties, plus impossibility results. Intractability remarks rely on prior work and are not main results.

C2.1.value: valuations; ordinal preference orders (translated to Borda valuations)
C2.1.quote: every agent i reports her valuation

C2.2.quote: each agent reports for every round a total order over C
C2.2.note: Cardinal valuations in general; strict rankings translated via Borda in the restricted setting.

C2.3.quote: We assume that the agents have additive utility functions.
C2.3.note: Utilities and preferences are attributed to agents.

C2.4.quote: every agent i reports her valuation
C2.4.note: The paper says each agent reports her own valuation and uses it directly as her utility, with no reason given. IDU is excluded because the paper does speak of reporting.

C3.1.quote: every agent i reports her valuation

C3.2.quote: every agent i reports her valuation
C3.2.note: Weak statement: the agent reports her own valuation.

C4.1.quote: the valuation of a candidate c is the number of candidates ranked below
C4.1.note: Borda translation defines utilities from rankings.

C4.2.quote: they assign either 1 or 0 to each candidate

C5.1.quote: An outcome o is Pareto Optimal (PO) if there does not
C5.1.note: Pareto optimality and proportionality (fairness to agents) are used in the results.

C5.2.quote: the accumulated utility of an agent i from outcome o
C5.2.note: Utilities are sums of reported valuations, which the paper says are the agents' own valuations.

VOT.quote_behav: every agent i reports her valuation
VOT.note: Reports are fixed inputs. In round robin, an agent's choice of a round is part of the mechanism definition and is not strategic.

claims.quote: a decision-making mechanism must consider fairness notions
has a significant advantage over the other known mechanisms
our results are also applicable when the preferences of the agents are ordinal

C9.2.quote: In these settings, we translate the ordinal preference orders
C9.2.note: Two assumptions are needed: that reports equal valuations, and that Borda valuations stand for utility when preferences are ordinal. Both are stated, the first only weakly ('reports her valuation').

C2.4.reason: The phrase 'reports her valuation' is a statement that the submitted input equals the agent's own valuation, given without a reason, so IDS applies; IDU requires that there be no statement about reporting.

C3.2.reason: Consistent with C2.4 = IDS, the paper says in words that agents report their own valuations.

C3.3.reason: C3.2 is STATED and the paper gives no reason for truthful reporting.

C5.2.reason: Fairness and efficiency are evaluated on the reported valuations, and the paper states (C2.4 = IDS) that these are the agents' valuations.

C9.2.reason: Given that the paper states truthful reporting (weakly) and the Borda translation, every needed assumption is stated.
